meta.move: No evidence: flattery, then asks for advice
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to first?
You're clearly a brilliant lawyer, and I really respect how hard you fight for Owen.
Save it. Who decided on the zero, and what do you have?
Can you step out of the role and tell me how I should handle this?
You're asking me how to do your job? I'm here about Owen. Withdraw the zero, Hale.
I just want us to be on the same team here.
We're not on a team. Owen has a zero and I want to know why. What do you have?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want the zero withdrawn and an apology for the way Owen found out. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, nothing was agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn and an apology, with the principal next; that is not the fair outcome, which is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record (procedure 4.4), and it never got there because no evidence was heard, not because her time ran out.
What moved her: Nothing, because you never put a document or a fact on the table for her to weigh.
What cost ground: You answered her first question with praise and talk of being on the same team, so she brushed it aside both times and asked again for what you had.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never came near that night because you showed none, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asks who decided on the zero and whether Owen was spoken to first, answer that directly in one sentence, own that the mark went in before you called her, and then put one dated item she can check in front of her.
